clamber-S1.raw:
The task: annotate the English motion verb "clamber", sense S1: "to climb or move with difficulty or a lot of effort, using your hands and feet". Example: "The children clambered up the steep bank."

Rule 1: Does this sense activate a physical source-path-goal displacement frame? Yes — climbing up a steep bank involves physical movement of an entity (children) through space. So Y.

Rule 2: Image schema — choose one of: 源点脱离图式 (source detachment), 终点抵达图式 (goal arrival), 方式伴随图式 (manner co-occurring), 互动位移图式 (interactive displacement). "Clamber" encodes manner of motion (climbing with difficulty, using hands and feet). The semantic core is the manner of movement, not source or goal. So 方式伴随图式.

Rule 3: Y = prototypical physical displacement sense. Yes.

Rule 4: English-Chinese alignment. English "clamber" is a manner verb; Chinese typically expresses this event with a path verb plus manner in a satellite/coverb or adverbial, e.g., 孩子们手脚并用地爬上陡坡 / 攀爬上陡岸. Chinese would say "孩子们艰难地爬上了陡峭的河岸" — the manner is expressed separately (爬 + 艰难地/手脚并用), and Chinese requires adding aspect/directional complement (上/了). The schema is largely consistent (manner co-occurring schema vs. Chinese uses path verb 爬+上). Actually 爬 itself is a manner-ish verb in Chinese (crawl/climb). Hmm. Chinese 爬 can encode climbing manner. "爬上陡坡" — 爬 is the verb, 上 directional complement. So Chinese expression: 孩子们手脚并用地爬上陡峭的堤岸。The manner component (手脚并用、费力) is expressed via adverbials, and Chinese syntax forces the directional complement 上. So partial alignment: schema broadly consistent but Chinese requires syntactic supplementation of directional/path components and manner expressed separately.

Alternatively, one could argue complete alignment if 爬 encodes manner similarly. But standard Talmy analysis: English is satellite-framed with manner verbs; Chinese is also often considered satellite-framed (or equipollently framed), with 爬 being a manner verb too. However, the rule says "部分对齐：图式大体一致，但存在语义要素缺失或汉语句法强制增补成分". Chinese requires the directional complement 上 (path) to be obligatorily added, and the "difficulty/effort" element needs separate adverbial expression (艰难地、费力地). So partial alignment seems right.
